title: Complaint of Hutchinson & Bulkeley v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery did not err by indefinitely suspending RE Neill Payne from office without also suspending him from the Sacraments; the complaint was not sustained.
first_summary: Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s decision to suspend RE Neill Payne indefinitely from office but not from the Sacraments. The SJC did not sustain the complaint because the BCO does not require suspension from office always to include suspension from the Sacraments. It deferred to Presbytery’s discretionary judgment concerning the appropriate censure.
summary: Hutchinson and Bulkeley challenged Presbytery’s decision to suspend RE Neill Payne indefinitely from office but not from the Sacraments. The SJC did not sustain the complaint: BCO 30-3 expressly permits suspension from office without sacramental suspension, and no provision requires both censures together. Because the appropriate censure involved discretion and judgment, the SJC deferred absent clear error. Authority to remove or increase Payne’s censure had returned to his Session.
